nodes.summary: For the stationary OU process and `s ≤ t`, the conditional law of `X t` given `X s = x` is `N(e^{-θ(t-s)} x, (σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θ(t-s)}))` for almost every `x`.
nodes.title: Transition law

nodes.summary: For a centered Gaussian process with `cov(X s, X t) = c Var(X s)`, the conditional law of `X t` given `X s = x` is `N(c x, Var(X t) - c² Var(X s))` for almost every `x`.
nodes.title: Conditional law of a Gaussian process at one time given another

nodes.summary: For the OU process started at `0` and `s ≤ t`, the conditional law of `X t` given `X s = x` is `N(e^{-θ(t-s)} x, (σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θ(t-s)}))` for almost every `x`.
nodes.title: Transition law

nodes.summary: For the stationary OU process and `s ≤ t`, `E[X t | F s] = e^{-θ(t-s)} X s`, where `F` is the natural filtration of `X`.
nodes.title: Mean reversion

nodes.summary: For a centered Gaussian process with `cov(X u, X t) = c cov(X u, X s)` for all `u ≤ s`, the conditional expectation of `X t` given the natural filtration at `s` is `c X s`.
nodes.title: Conditional expectation of a Gaussian process given its past

nodes.summary: For the OU process started at `0` and `s ≤ t`, `E[X t | F s] = e^{-θ(t-s)} X s`, where `F` is the natural filtration of `X`.
nodes.title: Mean reversion

nodes.summary: The pathwise solution is continuous when the driving path is.
nodes.title: Continuity of the pathwise Langevin solution

nodes.summary: A continuous solution of `x t = x₀ - θ ∫_0^t x + σ (w t - w 0)` on `t ≥ 0` equals `ouPathSolution θ σ x₀ w` there.
nodes.title: Uniqueness

nodes.summary: The OU process of `IsOrnsteinUhlenbeckFromZero` starts at `0` almost surely.
nodes.title: The Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process from zero starts at zero

nodes.summary: An Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0` exists for every `θ > 0` and `σ`.
nodes.title: Existence of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero

nodes.summary: There is a probability measure on paths `ℝ≥0 → ℝ` under which the coordinate process is a pre-Brownian motion (Kolmogorov extension of the Brownian finite-dimensional laws).
nodes.title: Existence of a pre-Brownian motion on path space

nodes.summary: A stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process exists for every `θ > 0` and `σ`.
nodes.title: Existence of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process

nodes.summary: Each `X t` of a stationary OU process is `N(0, σ² / (2θ))`.
nodes.title: Stationary law

nodes.summary: The one-time law of the OU process started at `0`: `X t ~ N(0, (σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θt}))`.
nodes.title: One-time law of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process from zero

nodes.summary: Covariance of the Wiener integrals `I_t = ∫_0^t e^{θu} dB_u`: for a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past and `θ ≠ 0`, `E[I_s I_t] = (e^{2θ (s ∧ t)} - 1) / (2θ)`, by the martingale property and the Itô isometry.
nodes.title: Covariance of the Wiener integrals

nodes.summary: For a Brownian motion `B`, `θ ≠ 0`, any real `σ`, and a start `X₀ ~ N(0, v)` independent of `B`, the process `X t = ouPathSolution θ σ X₀ B t` (`t ≥ 0`) is a Gaussian process with `E[X t] = 0` and `cov[X s, X t] = e^{-θ(s+t)} (v + σ² (e^{2θ (s ∧ t)} - 1) / (2θ))` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6).
nodes.title: The pathwise Langevin solution driven by Brownian motion is Gaussian

nodes.summary: The time change `σ e^{-θt} B((e^{2θt} - 1)/(2θ))` of a pre-Brownian motion is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0`.
nodes.title: Construction (Doob 1942)

nodes.summary: Driven by a Brownian motion and started at `0`, `ouPathSolution` is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6). No filtration and no measurability of the coordinates of `B` is assumed.
nodes.title: The pathwise Langevin solution is an OU process

nodes.summary: `X` is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0` with rate `θ > 0` and noise amplitude `σ` under `P`: a centered Gaussian process with covariance `ouCovariance θ σ`. Only the finite-dimensional laws are fixed (no path regularity).
nodes.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero

nodes.summary: Driven by a Brownian motion `B` and started from `X₀ ~ N(0, σ²/(2θ))` independent of `B`, `ouPathSolution` is a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6).
nodes.title: Stationary start

nodes.summary: The time change `σ e^{-θt} B(e^{2θt}/(2θ))` of a pre-Brownian motion is a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process.
nodes.title: Construction (Doob 1942)

nodes.summary: `X` is a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with rate `θ > 0` and noise amplitude `σ` under `P`: a centered Gaussian process with covariance `ouStationaryCovariance θ σ`. Only the finite-dimensional laws are fixed.
nodes.title: Stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process

nodes.summary: Elementary Itô integrals against two modifications of the same process agree almost surely.
nodes.title: Elementary Itô integrals agree for modifications

nodes.summary: The finite-dimensional laws of a real Gaussian process are determined by its mean and covariance functions: two Gaussian processes with the same means and covariances (possibly on different probability spaces) have the same finite-dimensional laws.
nodes.title: Gaussian process laws are determined by mean and covariance

nodes.summary: Every finite-dimensional law of a stationary OU process is invariant under time shifts.
nodes.title: Strict stationarity

nodes.summary: If `X₀` is a real Gaussian random variable independent of the real Gaussian process `B`, the process indexed by `Option T` that is `X₀` at `none` and `B t` at `some t` is a Gaussian process.
nodes.title: Adjoining an independent Gaussian variable

nodes.summary: Doob's clock `τ t = (e^{2θt} - 1)/(2θ)` for the process started at `0`. The value is nonnegative for every real `θ`, so `Real.toNNReal` only changes its type.
nodes.title: Doob's clock for the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process from zero

nodes.summary: The OU covariance is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck covariance

nodes.summary: The variance of the OU process started at `0`: `(σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θt})`.
nodes.title: Variance of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero

nodes.summary: The covariance function of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0`: `(σ² / (2θ)) (e^{-θ|t-s|} - e^{-θ(t+s)})` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6). It is meant for `θ > 0` and times `s, t ≥ 0`; at `θ = 0` the division by zero makes it `0`.
nodes.title: Covariance of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero

nodes.summary: Doob's time change `t ↦ σ e^{-θt} B(τ t)` of a process `B`, with `τ = ouClock θ`.
nodes.title: Doob's time change of Brownian motion

nodes.summary: For a continuous path `w` and every real `t`, `ouPathSolution θ σ x₀ w` satisfies `x t = x₀ - θ ∫_0^t x + σ (w t - w 0)` (any real `θ`, `σ`, `x₀`).
nodes.title: Pathwise Langevin equation

nodes.summary: The explicit solution of the pathwise Langevin equation driven by a path `w`: `e^{-θt} x₀ + σ (w t - e^{-θt} w 0 - θ ∫_0^t e^{-θ(t-u)} w u du)`. This is `e^{-θt} x₀ + σ ∫_0^t e^{-θ(t-u)} dw(u)` after integration by parts (the Itô-integral form for a Brownian path is a wanted statement).
nodes.title: Pathwise solution of the Langevin equation

nodes.summary: Doob's clock `t ↦ e^{2θt}/(2θ)` for the stationary process (positive for `θ > 0`).
nodes.title: Doob's clock for the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process

nodes.summary: The stationary variance `σ² / (2θ)`.
nodes.title: Variance of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process

nodes.summary: The covariance function of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process: `(σ² / (2θ)) e^{-θ|t-s|}` (Uhlenbeck–Ornstein 1930). It is meant for `θ > 0`.
nodes.title: Covariance of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process

nodes.summary: Doob's stationary time change `t ↦ σ e^{-θt} B(e^{2θt}/(2θ))` of a process `B`.
nodes.title: Doob's stationary time change of Brownian motion

nodes.summary: A time shift of a stationary OU process is a stationary OU process.
nodes.title: Time shifts of a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process

nodes.summary: For the process started at `0`, `cov(X (s + h), X (t + h)) → (σ² / (2θ)) e^{-θ|t-s|}` as `h → ∞`.
nodes.title: Relaxation to stationarity

nodes.summary: Shifting both times by `h → ∞` turns `ouCovariance` into `ouStationaryCovariance`.
nodes.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck covariance converges to the stationary one

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
